title: Context economics lab notes
content:
Quick sprint dump — thinking about simple heuristics we can operationalize to reduce token cost while keeping tail latency under control. Notes to self + questions for Maya/Samir.

Problem framing
- We serve mixed workloads: short prompts (10-50 tokens) and sporadic long sessions (1k-50k). Cost is per-token, but latency and KV cache behavior make the per-token "effective" cost non-linear.
- Goal: propose a small set of runtime heuristics (config knobs) that Platform can expose with low implementation complexity and measurable ROI.

High-level heuristics (candidate list)
1) Adaptive prefix compression (cheap): detect repeating prefix tokens across sessions within a minute window, store compressed prefix blobs and expand on the far edge. Hypothesis: saves 5-12% tokens for chatty flows. Implementation risk: minimal.
2) Micro-batching short synchronous requests: group <50-token requests for 10ms windows to improve utilization. Tradeoff: small added P95; big wins for throughput.
3) Eviction-awareness for KV cache: prefer evicting rarely-used long-key prefixes vs recently-used small prefixes. Heuristic = frequency*recency score.
4) Latency-tier routing: route user-tier=free to quantized lower-cost runtimes for non-critical prompts, with safe fallback to higher-quality model on hallucination signals.

Concrete experiment ideas
- EXP-ctx-001: Turn on micro-batching for a single tenant (low P95 SLO slack). Monitor token cost, P50/P95 latency, error rates. Duration 72h. Goal: net token cost delta and latency shift. Link to ticket: RI-1234.
- EXP-ctx-002: Prefix compression A/B: compare no-compress vs zstd-level2 blobs (store metadata in per-session index). Track compression ratio and rehydration CPU cost.

Quick back-of-envelope on batching window vs P95 tradeoff
- Assumptions: batch window 10ms -> average added queue delay ~5ms. For P95-sensitive flows (SLO 200ms), adding 5-10ms likely ok. For P99 in interactive tooling maybe not.
- Measure: request arrival distribution, tail quantiles pre-change, predicted tail shift = small for exponential arrivals but worse for heavy-tailed.

Open questions / risks
- Correctness of prefix compression when model uses position-dependent features or absolute position embeddings (need model-compat checks).
- Safety/quality regressions when routing to quantized variants; need lightweight regression hooks (small evals on live prompt set).
- Billing complexity: prefix compression may change token counts in billing. Coordinate with billing to ensure transparency.

Notes to self: evaluation harness
- Create a small replay harness that replays 48h of traffic for candidate tenant. Include tokens, user session IDs, timestamps. Patch runtime to simulate heuristics offline and compute expected token savings and latency deltas.
- For KV-eviction heuristic, instrument per-shard eviction events and compute "usefulness" metric: fraction of requests that hit rehydrated keys within 10s.

Draft rollout plan (minimal viable)
1) Local sim run for two heuristics (micro-batching + prefix compression) using replay harness. Produce metrics csv.
2) Canary (1% traffic) with feature flag and observability dashboard: per-tenant token rate, P50/P95/P99 latency, model errors, hallucination proxy (semantic mismatch metric).
3) 100% opt-in toggle for tenants with terms explaining possible quality vs cost tradeoffs.

Short list of reference reading (skimmed)
- "Efficient Transformers and Serving" (arXiv link above) — ideas on compression and KV lifetimes.
- Internal PR: serving-runtime/pull/482 — micro-batch queuer refactor (TODO: review code comments 2/3).
- Slack thread: #runtime-costs — has customer anecdote about long chat sessions causing high bill.

To-dos (next 7 days)
- [ ] Build replay harness scaffold (baseline + sim mode) — estimate 2 days.
- [ ] Prototype micro-batch scheduler variant (10ms windows) in a branch and run local load tests — 3 days.
- [ ] Discuss billing implications with Finance (Maya to intro) — 1 meeting.
- [ ] Prepare canary dashboard template (Samir) — simple Grafana panel list.

Quick heuristics cheat-sheet (for engs)
- If requests < 50 tokens: consider batching window 10ms, max batch 64.
- If session TTL < 30s and repeated prefixes detected: enable prefix compression.
- If tier=free or dev: route to 6-bit quantized model with fallback to full model on high-uncertainty signals.

Random scribbles / half-baked thoughts
- Could we do per-customer adaptive batching: higher batching for bursty tenants? Maybe set target throughput and back off window when latency spiking.
- Explore cheap ML classifier to flag "high-quality" prompts that should never route to quantized variants. Train on historical generation acceptance.

Questions for Maya/Samir meeting
- Which tenants are safe to test micro-batching on for 72h? (need list + contact).
- Do we have replay traffic snapshots or will infra provide an export?
- Does Finance want a conservative estimate before any canary?

Endnotes
- This doc is messy — intend to turn into a short proposal for the 1-week sprint review if experiments show promise.
- Save link in Eng Confluence under place-holder page: Confluence -> Runtime / Context Economics (will create if we proceed).
